name: read_uint1

name: read_uint2
reason: readUintN 2 mirrors :242-245; ReadUintExact pins the little-endian value for every n < 2**16 and a ValueError on fewer than two bytes. Only the class is pinned for uint2 (the message is existential there), unlike uint1/4/8.

reason: readInt4 mirrors :263-266; ReadInt4Exact pins every int struct.pack('<i') writes, negative ones included, and the exact :266 message on fewer than four bytes, so an unsigned or padding reader fails. Probed on 3.15.2: b'\x00\x00\x00\x80' gives -2147483648, b'\x05\x00' the message.

name: read_uint4

name: read_uint8
reason: readUintN 8 mirrors :305-308; ReadUintExact pins the value up to 2**64-1, and the count clauses of ReadBytesExact and ReadUnicodeExact pin the exact uint8 message.

name: read_stringnl
reason: readRawnl, stripQuotes and escapeDecode mirror :344-362 for the defaults, and ReadStringnlExact now pins repr lines with escapes undone, escape_decode of any quoted body, and the three ValueErrors (probed on 3.15.2: 30000 repr lines and random escape-heavy bodies agree, messages as stated). But the one-byte line `'` or `"` is in no clause (the body clause needs two quotes, onequote needs a different last byte): 3.15.2 returns '' there, and a reader that rejects a lone quote, as load_string does (python/cpython#127045), satisfies every clause. Add that line to the theorem.

name: read_stringnl_noescape
reason: readStringnlNoescape is readRawnl, escapeDecode and a strict UTF-8 decode, as `read_stringnl(f, stripquotes=False, encoding='utf-8')`; NoescapeNoBackslash pins every backslash-free line (decoded, or UnicodeDecodeError), and the refutation of NoescapeVerbatim, with its bug record, pins the backslash case, so a verbatim reader or one without the UTF-8 check fails.

name: read_stringnl_noescape_pair
reason: Two readStringnlNoescape calls joined by 0x20, as `"%s %s"` at :395; the second conjunct of NoescapeNoBackslash pins `u + ' ' + v` for two decodable lines, so dropping the space, swapping the order or reading one line fails.

Probed on 3.15.2: b'\x05ab' gives that message with 5 and 2.

name: read_bytes4

name: _genops
reason: genopStep and genopsLoop mirror :2305-2326 (citation now :2305-2323). GenopsExact pins one round at any position exactly: 'pickle exhausted before seeing STOP', 'at position %s, opcode %r unknown' with <unknown> without tell, and a known opcode with its reader's argument or exception and both positions; whole runs of argument-free opcodes with and without STOP; and the tell/no-tell twin. With GenopsWellFormed and GenopsFuelEnough an always-raising or position-skipping parse fails. Probed on 3.15.2: messages and positions as stated, with and without tell. Streams with FLOAT stop at the model's Excluded marker (read_floatnl is todo).

name: genops
reason: `return _genops(pickle)` (:2351); the same entries, and GenopsExact's notell clauses now state the documented `pos is None` case (:2345-2349): the same opcodes and arguments without positions, failing exactly when the bytes do.

name: optimize
reason: optStep and optEmit mirror :2365-2417 (citations now :2365-2387, :2399-2416; hasSub is now a structural substring test, equal to `in` on str, the empty needle included). OptimizeExact equates the model with a declarative output (header, every opcode but FRAME and unused PUTs, each kept PUT and GET renumbered to its key's rank, reframed from protocol 4), so keeping unused PUTs or not renumbering fails. MemoWF (distinct memo keys, GET after PUT) is the pickler's discipline: my transcription of the statement matched pickletools.optimize on 12000 pickle.dumps/_dumps outputs at protocols 0-5 (3 seeds, recursive and 70000-byte objects included), and every one satisfied MemoWF. Outside it only OptimizeGetNone's two examples are on record, and FLOAT streams are outside through genops' Excluded marker.

name: dis
reason: The model mirrors :2466-2592 and the citations are right. DisChecks pins each sanity check from any state with its exact message (probed on 3.15.2: every message as stated), and ReprOk is an honest scope limit (no check fires on float opcodes, PUT/GET ints cannot pass 4300 digits). But no entry states what a successful opcode does: the stack and memo effects (:2534, :2538, :2574-2584) and the printed line are unstated. So a dis that never stores PUTs into the memo, or never pushes stack_after, satisfies DisChecks, DisFollowsGenops and the refutation, while rejecting valid pickles such as b'(lp0\ng0\na.' or b'N.'. The checks after a MARK pop (b'(Nu.' gives 'tries to pop 1 items from stack with only 0 items') are also outside the pop clause.
